openings.claim: Replace timestamp-first scanning with a manifest-position boundary ledger and a targeted ambiguity check. This proposes evidence handling, not an explanation of the injected divergences.
openings.delta: A local script aligns supplied records by manifest identifiers and dictionary-defined artifact boundaries. It marks digest comparisons equal, unequal or unavailable; blank warnings remain blank. Equal recorded inputs with unequal recorded outputs support a stage-local mismatch. Unequal inputs point upstream. Report the earliest supported stage in expected-stage order only when earlier recorded boundaries are accounted for; otherwise report an explicit interval containing unresolved earlier boundaries. Keep execution-time ordering uncertainty separate, including the inverted export timestamp. Attach record identifiers to every definite claim. Rank available records for the next manual check by which could distinguish the earliest remaining alternatives; record every inspection and stop at twelve.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: timestamp-first scanning that stops at its first digest mismatch. The workflows may locate different candidate stages for the inverted-timestamp pair. After transform-record removal, the proposed ledger should preserve or widen its uncertainty, never infer nonexecution or gain certainty from missing evidence. These are predicted behaviors, not observed results.
openings.probe: Apply the proposal to one three-pair subset and the rival to the disjoint subset within sixty analyst minutes. Freeze referenced outputs and inspection logs before opening the two sealed answer sheets. Use twenty additional minutes to compare supported locations, interval containment of injected boundaries, ordering-sensitive decisions and inspection counts. Review the stipulated record removals with manifests unchanged. Disjoint subsets permit a feasibility and error-description probe, not a controlled performance claim.
assumptions: The dictionary and manifest permit matching artifact boundaries; ambiguity remains unresolved if they do not.

Defeat conditions include incomparable digests, inconsistent identifiers or an interval that excludes the sealed boundary. Exhausting twelve inspections yields an unresolved result and a next check naming an available record, not an extra inspection.

A time cap alone does not establish feasibility; actual completion and logs must show that six referenced reports and resource-fitting next checks were produced. No live access or reliable effect is assumed.

assessment: One resource-bounded proposal. Recorded-boundary support and actual execution chronology remain distinct; sealed answers test the proposal after freezing, without licensing invented observations.
